title: Native CSS Week: Starting Styles, Anchors, Drop Caps & Auto-Height
description: Five browser-native CSS/JS platform features doing UI work third-party libraries used to own: entrances, anchoring, type, reorder, and height.

drops.title: Native CSS Entry & Exit Animations
drops.description: Toasts, a popover menu and a bottom sheet all animate into and out of display:none using nothing but CSS.
drops.concept: @starting-style defines the frame an element animates FROM the instant it stops being display:none, while transition-behavior: allow-discrete lets the discrete display property itself participate in the transition. Together they replace the JS library trick of keeping a hidden element mounted-but-invisible: the element genuinely isn't in the render tree until it opens, and genuinely leaves it again on close, with a real two-way animation both ways.

interaction.mouse: Click 'Fire a toast', 'Options', or 'Open sheet' to trigger each entry/exit pair
interaction.click: Same as mouse — every trigger is a button
interaction.touch: Tap any trigger button; menu/backdrop dismiss on outside tap

drops.title: CSS Anchor-Positioned Tooltips
drops.description: Three tooltips tether to their buttons purely in CSS, with one live-following an anchor inside a scrollable box.
drops.concept: anchor-name tags a reference element and position-anchor tethers a second element to it; the anchor() function then reads that anchor's own edges directly inside top/left/right/bottom, and position-try-fallbacks supplies an automatic flip when the tooltip would overflow the viewport. This is the declarative replacement for Floating UI / Popper-style JS positioning libraries — no ResizeObserver, no scroll listener, no manual recalculation.
drops.source: MDN Web Docs — 'Using CSS anchor positioning'

interaction.mouse: Hover any of the three buttons, or scroll the box to watch the corner tooltip re-tether
interaction.click: Focus a button with keyboard Tab to also reveal its tooltip
interaction.touch: Tap a button to toggle its tooltip open

drops.title: CSS initial-letter Drop Caps
drops.description: Three magazine-style drop caps sized and sunk by initial-letter's line-count math instead of a hand-tuned float.
drops.concept: initial-letter: <size> <sink> tells the browser exactly how many lines tall the capital should render and how many lines it sinks into the paragraph, laying it out against the real line box instead of the float-plus-font-size-guess hack developers have used for decades. This demo shows a classic 3-line drop cap, an oversized 5-line gradient-filled capital, and a compact 2-line 'raised' variant, all tunable live via the debug panel.
drops.source: DigitalOcean Community Tutorials — 'Drop Caps in CSS Using ::first-letter & initial-letter'

interaction.mouse: Drag the size/sink sliders to reshape the first card's drop cap live

drops.title: Reorder Lists with View Transitions
drops.description: Shuffle, sort, or drag the list and every displaced row morphs to its new slot instead of jumping there.
drops.concept: document.startViewTransition() snapshots every element carrying a view-transition-name before a DOM mutation, runs the callback that actually reorders the array, then snapshots the new layout and lets the browser animate each row's position, size and crossfade automatically — no manual FLIP transform math. The source article adds a playful skateboard-trick keyframe spin to the moved item's icon mid-transition; this demo echoes that with a 'kick flip' rotate-and-scale flourish on the grip icons every time a shuffle, sort, send-to-bottom, or drag reorder fires.
drops.source: Chris Coyier — 'View Transition List Reordering (with a Kick Flip)'

interaction.mouse: Click a toolbar button, or click-drag any row by its grip to reorder
interaction.click: Shuffle / send-to-bottom / sort buttons each trigger a morph
interaction.touch: Drag rows by touch; toolbar buttons are tap targets

drops.title: Auto-Height Accordions via calc-size()
drops.description: An FAQ accordion, an expandable card, and a toggle-all list all animate to a real content height with plain CSS.
drops.concept: interpolate-size: allow-keywords opts intrinsic sizing keywords like auto into being animatable at all, and calc-size(auto, size) lets that auto value be combined with arithmetic (e.g. size + 4px) while staying animatable — so a plain transition: height animates all the way to the element's true rendered height, no JS scrollHeight measurement, no ResizeObserver, no layout thrash on every keystroke of content change.

interaction.mouse: Click any FAQ question, the release-notes card, or a changelog row to expand/collapse
interaction.click: Same as mouse — every header is a toggle button
interaction.touch: Tap any header row to expand/collapse
